cisceNodes: c3_evs_001 (Living and non-living things - identification), c3_evs_002 (Plants and animals - basic differences and similarities), c3_evs_003 (External body parts of humans and animals)
mascotDescription: a friendly nature explorer with a magnifying glass, a backpack, a sun hat, and binoculars. Custom SVG, not an owl.
sceneDescription: nature park scene with sky gradient, trees, a pond, a dog, a bird, a stone, and a bench
challengeTypes: identify: Which of these is a LIVING thing? (A tree that grows vs A stone that stays the same vs A bench that gets old)
identify: Which of these is a NON-LIVING thing? (A chair vs A cat vs A rose plant)
sort: Drag each thing to Living or Non-Living (Living: tree, dog, bird, fish, plant, human | Non-Living: stone, bench, water, chair, pencil, fan)
identify: Which is a similarity between plants and animals? (Both are living things that grow vs Both can talk vs Both have legs)
sort: Drag each feature to Plant or Animal (Plant: makes own food, has leaves, cannot move from place, has roots | Animal: eats food, can move, has legs or wings, has eyes and ears)
identify: Which external body part do we use to SEE? (Eyes vs Ears vs Nose)
sort: Drag each body part to its function (Eyes: see | Ears: hear | Nose: smell | Tongue: taste | Skin: touch | Hands: hold and write | Legs: walk and run)
sort: Drag each body part to Human or Animal or Both (Human: hands for writing, talks with mouth | Animal: paws, tail, fur | Both: eyes, ears, nose, legs, heart)
extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Living and non-living identification — living things grow, need food and water, breathe, move on their own, reproduce, and die. Non-living things do not. Examples: living = tree, dog, bird, fish, plant, human. Non-living = stone, bench, water, chair, pencil, fan. Movement alone does not mean living (fan moves but is not living). (2) Plants and animals differences and similarities — similarities: both are living, both grow, both reproduce, both need food and water, both die. Differences: plants make own food (photosynthesis), animals eat food; plants cannot move from place to place, animals can move; plants have leaves and roots, animals have legs/wings/eyes; plants breathe through leaves, animals breathe through lungs or gills. (3) External body parts of humans and animals — humans: eyes (see), ears (hear), nose (smell), tongue (taste), skin (touch), hands (hold/write), legs (walk/run), mouth (eat/talk), teeth (chew), hair (protect head). Animals: eyes, ears, nose, mouth, legs (or wings/fins), tail (balance), fur/scales/skin (protection), paws/hooves/claws. Both humans and animals have eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and legs. Misconceptions: 'plants are not living because they don't move' (plants are living — they grow, need water, breathe, and reproduce; they just can't move from place to place), 'fan is living because it moves' (fan is non-living — it moves because of electricity, not on its own), 'animals and plants have nothing in common' (both are living, both grow, both need food and water, both reproduce), 'only humans have eyes and ears' (animals also have eyes, ears, and nose — many animals have better senses than humans). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function LivingEVSGame), NOT export default. Export interface LivingEVSGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void.
